# Patched dependency delivery probe

Runtime: Bun 1.4.0 (34cbb9a40). No publication, repository edits or other runtime.
Input: /tmp/acme-m03-packed-w8qBCv/acmelabs-design-system-0.2.0.tgz.

## Result

| Metadata/files in dependency tarball | Fresh local-tarball install | Fresh loopback-registry install | Installed lit-store patch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both patch entries and both patch files | Fails: patch path not found | Succeeds | Absent after registry install |
| Runtime patch entry and patch files | Fails: patch path not found | Succeeds | Absent after registry install |
| No patchedDependencies metadata | Succeeds | Succeeds | Absent |

The fixture pins lit-store to 0.13.2 so patch absence cannot be explained by a semver update. File hashes/source checks and reconnect browser outcomes verify the installed behavior.

Diagnostic only: copying patches into the local-tarball CONSUMER root allows installation and applies the runtime patch, without adding patchedDependencies to the consumer manifest. This shows that local-tarball handling resolves those patch paths against the wrong delivery boundary for a published library. This is not a proposed consumer requirement. All registry consumers remain independent of those copied files.

## Recommendation

Guarantee reconnect behavior in owned library helpers rather than depending on a transitive package-manager patch. Remove the runtime patch once that behavior has an independent regression test against unpatched upstream code. Keep the analyzer patch in the development checkout, but omit development patchedDependencies from staged production package metadata. Use the same staged package for pack verification and eventual publication. Simply adding patch files does not meet the consumer contract.

The M00 delivery fixture used an explicit patchedDependencies entry in its consumer/package.json plus its consumer/patches/lit-store.patch. It established mounting and bundle feasibility with a patched consumer, not delivery of a patch from a transitive package. That is the boundary this probe corrects.

## Files

- probe.ts: extract original package; create and pack the three metadata variants; install clean local-tarball consumers.
- results.json and original-manifest-subset.json: exact local-install outcomes/configuration.
- registry-and-root-probe.ts: serve immutable variant tarballs from a loopback-only registry, install fresh consumers, then run the consumer-root path diagnostic; shuts down the server.
- registry-results.json: exact registry and diagnostic outcomes.
- reconnect.ts: bundle directly from the actual installed dependency trees and exercise initial update, DOM reparenting, and the next store update in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit; closes browsers/server.
- reconnect-results.json: browser outcomes.
- Each variant directory contains its staged package, tarball, consumer manifests/locks, pack log and original install log. Registry consumers have their own .npmrc scoped only to the loopback registry. No account credentials were used.

## Official guidance checked

https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/patch documents project patch files, package.json/lockfile entries and applying patches to dependencies. It does not establish published-library transitive patch behavior. The install/browser probes above are the evidence for that boundary. No claim is made about other Bun versions or package managers.

## Development-patch boundary

An analyzer-only package variant installs successfully when the consumer has no analyzer dependency: an unused development patch does not alone force analyzer installation. When the consumer independently installs analyzer 0.11.0, however, Bun 1.4.0 crashes with SIGABRT and `Option::unwrap()` on `None` for that local-tarball metadata. This reproduced in two fresh directories. The equivalent consumer with the no-patch-config tarball installs 128 packages successfully. These are Bun-version-specific observations, not a diagnosis of Bun's internal cause.

Files: analyzer-only/results.json, analyzer-only/consumer-with-analyzer-results.json, analyzer-only/consumer-with-analyzer-fresh-results.json, no-patch-config/consumer-with-analyzer-results.json. dev-patch-probe.ts reproduces the two failing cases plus the clean control in fresh directories. The analyzer-only tarball preserves the exact existing development patch and excludes the runtime patch entry.

# Root package / child workspace linkage

Verified Bun 1.4.0. Scratch only. No global bun link registration or project edits.

Selected approach: preserve required exact core peers in child packages; keep root's local override `core-name: file:.`; configure the project-local bunfig.toml with `[install] linker = "hoisted"`. The production staging manifest must omit the local override.

## Results

- Hoisted: node_modules/@acme/root-probe is a symlink to the actual root (`../..`). Three packages resolve the same root/dist/index.js and share exactly the same exported object identity as a direct root import.
- Initial clean install, fully clean frozen reinstall, and repeated frozen reinstall without cleanup all pass. Lock remains unchanged during final frozen verification.
- Deleting/recreating the entire dist directory preserves live resolution. Runtime and bundled output both report the rebuilt value from all three packages. Bun metafiles show one actual root/dist module.
- Isolated: its package-local symlink targets the installed `.bun/...@root/...` copy. In-place edits can appear through shared file backing, but deleting/recreating dist leaves stale output. `--backend symlink` does not correct this. Do not call this a live root link.
- Relative `link:../..` in a child requests global registration. Listing `.` as a workspace does not make workspace:* resolve root. Neither is selected.

## Transition failure

The older single-workspace fixture was expanded and reinstalled without fully clearing its prior package-local installation state. A nested core link under packages/react pointed at `../..` (the React directory), shadowing the correct root link and breaking imports. Its files/lock remain in override-file-hoisted. This is not reproduced by the clean three-workspace fixture. Changing linkers needs a clean reinstall of root and package-local node_modules and an actual-root-resolution regression check; an install exit code alone is insufficient.

## Reproduce

- `bun probe.ts`: initial protocol/linker matrix, results.json.
- `bun fresh-three.ts`: creates a new three-workspace fixture, runs initial and clean frozen installs, checks rebuild/runtime/bundler, writes fresh-three-results.json with full metafiles.
- `bun final-verification.ts`: repeated frozen reinstall and runtime/bundled singleton check; writes final-verification.json and exits nonzero on failure.

`verify-hoisted.ts` preserves the transition experiment; it is expected to expose that earlier contaminated state. An optional-peer/file-devDependency alternative finished before the stop instruction and is recorded in probe-alternative.ts/alternative-results.json; it is not the selected recommendation, because required production peer semantics should remain intact.

## Official sources

- https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig#installlinker explicitly supports project-local `[install] linker = "hoisted"`.
- https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install#installation-strategies describes hoisted versus isolated installation.
- https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install#overrides-and-resolutions documents root dependency overrides.
- https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/link documents registered linkable packages; no global registration was used here.
- https://bun.com/docs/pm/workspaces documents child workspace references and packaging rewrites. The root behavior above is established by executable evidence, not assumed from the workspace examples.

No server or browser processes were started for this investigation.
